module


public import Mathlib.Algebra.Squarefree.Basic

@[expose] public section

variable {M M₀ : Type*} {r m : M} {k : ℕ}

section Monoid
variable [Monoid M]

def Powerfree (k : ℕ) (m : M) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃x : M⦄, x ^ k ∣ m → IsUnit x

theorem Powerfree.of_le {a b : ℕ} (hab : a ≤ b) (hm : Powerfree a m) :
  Powerfree b m := fun x hx => hm (dvd_of_mul_right_dvd (pow_mul_pow_sub x hab ▸ hx))

theorem Powerfree.of_dvd (hrm : r ∣ m) (hm : Powerfree k m) :
    Powerfree k r := fun _ hx => hm (hx.trans hrm)

theorem powerfree_congr (hrm : Associated r m) : Powerfree k r ↔ Powerfree k m :=
  ⟨fun h => h.of_dvd hrm.dvd', fun h => h.of_dvd hrm.dvd⟩

@[simp]
theorem powerfree_neg [HasDistribNeg M] : Powerfree k (-m) ↔ Powerfree k m :=
  powerfree_congr (Associated.refl m).neg_left

@[simp]
theorem powerfree_two {m : M} : Powerfree 2 m ↔ Squarefree m where
  mp h x hx := h (sq x ▸ hx)
  mpr h x hx := h x (sq x ▸ hx)

end Monoid

section CommMonoid
variable [CommMonoid M]

theorem IsUnit.powerfree (h : IsUnit m) (hk : k ≠ 0) :
    Powerfree k m := fun _ hx => (isUnit_pow_iff hk).1 (isUnit_of_dvd_unit hx h)

@[simp]
theorem powerfree_one (hk : k ≠ 0) : Powerfree k (1 : M) :=
  isUnit_one.powerfree hk

theorem Irreducible.powerfree (h : Irreducible m) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    Powerfree k m := by
  rintro y ⟨z, hz⟩
  induction k with
  | zero => grind
  | succ n ih =>
  rw [pow_succ, mul_assoc] at hz
  rcases h.isUnit_or_isUnit hz with (hu | hu)
  · exact (isUnit_pow_iff (by linarith)).1 hu
  · apply isUnit_of_mul_isUnit_left hu

end CommMonoid

@[simp]
theorem not_powerfree_zero [MonoidWithZero M₀] [Nontrivial M₀] (k : ℕ) :
    ¬ Powerfree k (0 : M₀) := by
  rw [Powerfree, not_forall]
  exact ⟨0, by simp⟩

theorem Prime.powerfree [CommMonoidWithZero M₀] [IsCancelMulZero M₀] {m : M₀} (h : Prime m)
    (hk : 2 ≤ k) : Powerfree k m := h.irreducible.powerfree hk

findings.description: In FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/978.lean:56–58, the conclusion uses Powerfree (f.natDegree - 2), but hp only excludes fixed prime powers with exponent f.natDegree - 1. This does not exclude the fixed divisors that obstruct the actual Powerfree predicate. A counterexample is f(X) = ∏_{i=0}^8 (X-i) + 256X^3 + 384. It is monic, irreducible by Eisenstein at 3, and has degree 9. Its value f(0)=384=2^7·3 witnesses hp for every prime, since no prime eighth power divides 384. Nevertheless, 2^7 divides every f(n), so the asserted infinite set is empty. All these facts, including a refutation of the declaration's universally quantified statement, were proved in /workspace/review/counterexample9.lean using only standard Lean axioms. The library definition Powerfree itself is correct.
findings.source_evidence: Browning, Power-free values of polynomials, introduction and the paragraph following Theorem 1 (manuscript pp. 1–2), defines a fixed kth-power divisor by a prime p satisfying p^k ∣ f(n) for every n. The infinitude of (d−2)-free values for d≥9 is explicitly conditional on the absence of that obstruction: https://web.archive.org/web/20110401122225id_/http://www.maths.bris.ac.uk/~matdb/preprints/powerfree.pdf . The cited problem page likewise explicitly requires that there be no prime p with p^(k−2) ∣ f(n) for all n, calling this an obvious necessary condition: https://www.erdosproblems.com/978 .
findings.suggested_fix: Replace f.natDegree - 1 by f.natDegree - 2 in hp: (hp : ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 2) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)). Mention this local condition in the docstring. Leave Powerfree and the research solved category unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The definition quantifies over all monoid elements and requires a kth-power divisor's base to be a unit. Number-theoretic sources usually exclude prime kth-power divisors or positive nontrivial kth powers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On ℕ and ℤ, every nonunit has a positive prime divisor. If x^k divides m and p divides x, then p^k divides m. Conversely, a prime kth-power divisor directly violates Powerfree because a prime is not a unit. Integer divisibility is invariant under signs, and the integer units are precisely ±1. Scratch proofs establish the prime-power characterization on both ℕ and ℤ, and Powerfree k n.natAbs ↔ Powerfree k n for integers, including zero and the degenerate exponents. The existing powerfree_two theorem also agrees exactly with Mathlib's general-monoid Squarefree definition.

reformulations.difference: Compared with the first question on erdosproblems.com/978, the Lean statement explicitly adds the absence of fixed prime (d−1)st-power divisors.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This hypothesis follows from the other assumptions. An irreducible nonconstant integer polynomial is primitive. Erdős's 1953 paper, p. 417, recalls that every fixed divisor of a primitive degree-d polynomial divides d!. For primes p≥3, v_p(d!)≤(d−1)/(p−1)<d−1. For p=2, v_2(d!)=d−s₂(d)≤d−2 because d is not a power of 2. Thus no p^(d−1) can divide all values, and adding the explicit local hypothesis does not weaken the stated question. The primitivity implication was checked in Lean; the complete fixed-divisor equivalence was not formalized in the scratch files.
